title: ～のに — “even though ～” (against expectation)
summary: Used when the result goes against what you expected. It follows the plain form (noun and na-adjective take なのに) and carries feelings of surprise, complaint or regret.

patterns.gloss: Verbs and i-adjectives stay in plain form (勉強したのに / 寒いのに)

patterns.form: 名詞・な形容詞＋なのに
patterns.gloss: Nouns and na-adjectives take な (春なのに / 静かなのに)

body.p: It joins two real facts where the second is the opposite of what the first would lead you to expect: 頑張ったのに落ちた (I tried hard, yet I failed). Both parts are things that actually happened or are true.
The speaker usually feels surprise, annoyance or regret. After のに you cannot place a command, request or intention (～てください, ～しよう). For a neutral “but”, use が or けれど instead.

examples.ja: 一生懸命（いっしょうけんめい）勉強（べんきょう）したのに、試験（しけん）に落（お）ちました。
examples.romaji: Isshōkenmei benkyō shita noni, shiken ni ochimashita.
examples.tr: Even though I studied hard, I failed the exam.

examples.ja: もう春（はる）なのに、まだ寒（さむ）い。
examples.romaji: Mō haru na noni, mada samui.
examples.tr: Even though it is already spring, it is still cold.

examples.ja: 薬（くすり）を飲（の）んだのに、熱（ねつ）が下（さ）がらない。
examples.romaji: Kusuri o nonda noni, netsu ga sagaranai.
examples.tr: Even though I took medicine, my fever won't go down.

pitfalls: With nouns and na-adjectives use なのに, not だのに (春なのに).
Do not follow のに with a request, command or intention (× 勉強したのに、手伝ってください).
